t: Signing up and creating the account
s: How to create your login, and then the account that brings your venues together.
h: Your login The account Look at the example The trial
b: Signing up takes two steps. First you create your own login, then the account that holds your venues, your team and the daily report. You won't need a bank card. On the sign-in page, press the Open an account button. Type your email address in the Email field. Choose a password of at least 8 characters in the Password field, then type it again in Password again. Press the Sign up button. Under the button, it says that by signing up you accept the terms of service and acknowledge the privacy notice. You can open both from there. On the Create your account page, type the name of your venue or company in the Account name field. You can rename it later. Check the Time zone field. We fill it in from your browser, but you can change it. In the Language field, choose the language for your daily report. Press the Create account button. The First steps guide then opens on its own. It walks you through adding a venue and setting up the daily report. Tip: If a colleague has invited you to an existing account, don't create a new one. Sign up from the invitation link and you'll land in the right account straight away. While your account has no venue, you can open Nézd meg a példát (look at the example) from the empty screens and the set-up guide. The 3 example screens are Ma (today), Válaszok (replies) and Kimutatások (reports). They use invented data and carry the Példa label, meaning example. None of it is saved. As an owner, Add your first venue takes you back to adding your first venue. A new account starts with a 14-day trial. The article about the trial explains what's included and where to see how many days you have left.

s: Find your restaurant on Google, add it, and a few minutes later you'll see its latest reviews.
h: How to add it Sharing a Google Maps link What you see next What we download first If you get stuck If Google can no longer find it If you want to pause a venue
b: The account owner adds venues. You add the first one in the First steps guide and any others on the Venues page, using the same card. Open the Venues page. It's in the Your venues group of the left-hand rail, or under More on a phone. In a new account, the First steps guide opens by itself instead. On the Add venue card, type the venue's name, with the city if you like, for example “Példa Bisztró Budapest”. Press the Search button. Instead of the name, you can also paste the long Google Maps link or the place id. Then you get one row, with “Here's the place we found from the link.” (or “…for that id.”) above it. In the results, check the address and the number of reviews, so you're sure you're picking your own venue. Press the Add button. The First download card shows how far the download has got. First it shows the review count and average that Google displays, then how many reviews we've downloaded. It usually takes a minute or two, and you can carry on with the next step of the guide in the meantime. On Android, if you've installed the app on your phone, you can send a Google Maps link straight to the app from Maps' Share menu. The Venues page opens and the search runs with the link. Until your first daily report is ready, the Today tab works from the downloaded reviews. The Reviews downloaded, Their average and Waiting for a reply tiles show how many reviews we downloaded, their average, and how many written replies are waiting for you. A line above them also tells you when negative reviews from the last 30 days are waiting for a reply. In the meantime, we write replies to the recent reviews that don't have one yet, except 4- and 5-star reviews with no text. You'll find those replies on the Replies tab. The venue's latest reviews, not its whole history. We don't write replies to the older reviews. You can see them on the Reviews tab. The daily report doesn't count the older reviews from the first download as new. Your first daily report comes at the hour you set. If that hour's already passed today, it comes tomorrow. If there are no results, the profile may not be verified yet, may have no public address, or the place may be closed. Try the long Google Maps link or the place id. A short share link (maps.app.goo.gl, g.page or a Business Profile share link) doesn't say which place it is; the page tells you so and asks for the long link, the id, or the name and city. If a result says “Already on the list”, you've already added that venue. If a result says No public address, you can't add it here. We don't add places with no address on the map. Google says it's permanently closed: a permanently closed place can't be added. Google says it's temporarily closed is only a note, and the venue can still be added. If the venue is already in another account, the page says: “You can't add this restaurant right now. If it's yours, write to us through the Feedback button and we'll look into it.” If your current plan has no room for another venue, the page will tell you. Then write to us. If the download fails, we'll try again in the morning. You don't need to do anything. Tip: Linking your Google Business Profile is a separate step. You don't need it to download reviews, but you do need it to post replies. Adding us as a manager on Google shows you how. For a venue you've already added, A Google nem találja, meaning Google can't find it, signals a problem with its Google place ID. The account owner can use Keresd meg újra, meaning search again, on the Beállítás tab, meaning setup, to look for its current ID. If Google returns a new ID, we ask you to confirm the change. If it returns the same ID, we wait for the next check. If Google no longer recognises the ID, the search opens so you can choose the venue again. Your reviews and numbers stay. On the Venues page, click the venue's row and open its Setup tab. On the We're watching this venue card, turn the switch off and confirm with Switch off. While it's off, we don't download its reviews and it drops out of the daily report. Nothing's lost, and you can switch it back on at any time.

s: Waiting replies, reminders and changes worth a look.
h: Waiting replies and reminders Replies that didn't go out Improved ratings What increased A lower Google rating Cases and waves
b: Ma (Today) shows waiting replies, open reminders and changes at your venues. The 3 vár hétfő óta line, meaning 3 waiting since Monday, shows how many replies are waiting and at which venue the oldest one is. Replies put aside are counted separately, but putting them aside doesn't reduce the total waiting count. Reminders set with Emlékeztess (remind me) also appear here while they're open. See Later, hand over and reminders for more on putting replies aside and setting reminders. The didn't go out card lists approved replies that couldn't be posted. Each has a reason and a next step. A reply can get stuck because we don't have Google access to the venue or that access was removed. Other reasons include the review not being on Google, the review changing, or Google refusing the reply. Tap a row to get to Replies, where you can post the reply to Google by hand. Posting a reply by hand covers the steps. Javult az értékelés a válaszunk után (the rating improved after our reply) shows reviews whose stars went up after our reply. That's an observation, not proof that the reply caused the improvement. Ami megugrott (what increased) appears only when there's something to show. It carries the Az elmúlt 7 napban (in the last 7 days) tag. It shows a complaint theme with at least 5 complaints in the last 7 days, at least twice its own weekly average over the 8 weeks before, or a dish with 3 negative mentions. Tap a line to open that venue's reviews from the same 7 days. Esett a Google-értékelés (the Google rating fell) also appears only when there's something to show, with the Az elmúlt 7 napban (in the last 7 days) tag. The card's line says what the rating was a week ago and what it is today. If the latest check was yesterday, it says yesterday where it says today. Opening it takes you to the venue's page. You can hide or move these two cards in the edit mode on Ma (Today). New cards sit at the end until you set the order. Ügyek és hullámok (cases and waves) appears only when there's something to show. It flags an active wave, a case filed 14 days ago without an answer, or a venue closed on Google. Owners can also see a waiting invitation. You can move or hide this card too.

t: Adding us as a manager on Google
s: Add us as a manager on your Google Business Profile. Once we've accepted the invitation, we'll post the replies you approve.
h: The address you add On Google How the connection is going While the invitation is waiting Checking Until it is linked Taking the access back
b: You'll get your reviews without it. Manager access does two things. It lets us post your approved replies on Google, and it lets the Listing page see your Business Profile. The account owner goes through these steps. Open the Venues page and press the Check connection button. If any venue isn't linked yet, the Linking to Google Business Profile card appears. It shows the email address to add as a manager, and what to do In three steps. Copy the address. Open your Google Business Profile with the Google account you use to manage it as its owner. In the profile's settings, find the users and add a new one with the address you copied. Pick manager as the role and send the invitation. Google emails us the invitation. For now we accept these by hand, so the link won't work straight away. It starts working once we've accepted. On the venue's Beállítás tab, meaning setup, the Hol tartunk card, meaning where things stand, shows 4 checks. A Google-on van means the venue is on Google. A kezelőnk hozzáadva means our manager has been added. Válaszolhatunk means we can reply. Él a kapcsolat means the connection is working. Where something is still missing, its next step is beside it. Below the card, a line shows when we last read the reviews and whether that was through the Google API or Apify. It also tells you if there hasn't been a read yet. The card doesn't show whether Google has verified the profile. We don't read that information. Every night we check the invitations sent to our manager account. If we can see your venue's invitation, the line shows how many days it's been waiting. It also says the connection will become Összekapcsolva, meaning linked, once we've accepted. If you've waited at least 3 days and we can't see an invitation, the line asks you to check in the Google profile that you sent it. A person accepts the invitation; it isn't automatic. Go back to the Venues page and press Check connection again. Look at the venue's row in the table. If the Link column says Linked, you're done. Until we've accepted the invitation, it says Waiting to be accepted. You see the same on the venue's page, in the Google link part of its Setup tab. The five states: Linked: approve a reply and we'll post it on Google. Waiting to be accepted means the connection is waiting for the invitation to be accepted. Not linked: you post your replies on Google yourself. We lost access: our manager was removed from the Google profile. Until you add us back, you post replies by hand. Google can't find it: Google can't find a profile under this id. Check on Google that the place is still there. If it still says Not linked, press Check connection again later. If it still hasn't changed, let us know with the Feedback button. On a computer, click your name at the foot of the left-hand rail; on a phone, it's at the bottom of More. Nothing stops in the meantime. We still write the reply and you approve it. Then you copy it with one button and paste it in on Google yourself. Here's how: Posting a reply by hand, without Google access. You can remove our manager access on your Google Business Profile whenever you like. As soon as a reply can't go out because of it, or at the next check, the venue says We lost access by itself, and from then on you post replies by hand. The Today tab shows a notice too, We lost manager access on Google, with the steps, a link here and The venue's settings button. We also check access every night. If our manager can no longer see your venue's Google profile, the venue is unlinked. The owner gets one message about it on the alert channel. Add our manager again so you can post replies from here again.

s: Pick the time your daily report arrives, and connect Telegram if you'd like it there too.
h: The time Connecting Telegram Quiet hours and your personal copy Without Telegram The other two destinations
b: Every day at the time you set, the daily report sums up the reviews posted since the previous report, venue by venue. You can always read it in the app, and if you connect Telegram, we'll send it there too. The account owner sets the report's time and connects the account's Telegram chats. Open Értesítések, the notifications page. On the Daily report time card, pick the time. You can choose any quarter of an hour. Below it you'll see what time the report goes out, and in which time zone. The choice is saved at once, and Saved appears next to it. A new account gets its report at 08:00 in the morning, in the account's time zone. Under the morning report, you'll also see its last delivery. The line tells you when it went, which channel it used and whether it arrived. If quiet hours are holding it, you'll see when it's due. If delivery failed, you'll see why. On the same page, on the Telegram destinations card, press Connect in the Daily report row. If the report's for you, press the Open it on Telegram link and start the chat in Telegram. If it's for your team's group, add the Telegram account named on the panel to that group. Then send the command shown on the panel in the group. The Copy button copies it for you. When the code comes through, the panel shows which chat it came from. If that's the right one, press Yes, there. The code works for 10 minutes. If it's run out, press Connect again. Use Send a test message under your own Telegram chat to check the connection. You get one line back. You can request up to 5 tests an hour per login. Owners can also request a test and see the last message's status under the account's chats. The group chat of some accounts only receives the reports, with no test messages. Under Csendes órák (quiet hours), the Use different quiet hours on my devices switch sets a separate window for your devices. If you leave it off, the same quiet hours apply to both. Read Alerts for the details. The morning report itself isn't held back by quiet hours. If alerts waited during quiet hours, your personal copy of the morning report also has a line saying how many alerts we held back, with the affected venues. If you don't connect anything, the report is still made at the time you set. You'll find it on the Sent messages page, in the Account group of the left-hand rail or under More on a phone, marked “Here only. No Telegram chat is connected.” Want your phone to let you know when it arrives? See Putting it on your phone. We aren't sending reports by email now. On Értesítések, the notifications page, Levélben, meaning by mail, shows Hamarosan, meaning coming soon. The Marketing destination gets the weekly rank summary, and Alerts gets the alerts. You connect both the same way. There's more in Alerts. Tip: Got a question? Ask it on the Assistant page, in the Your venues group of the left-hand rail, or under More on a phone. It answers from your own reviews. More in The assistant.

s: BistroTech opens like an app from your home screen and can send you notifications.
h: On Android On iPhone The test notification The number on the icon Which account sent it Buttons on the notification Sound on this device Press and hold the icon Sharing into BistroTech The /app address Without internet Undoing an action
b: There's nothing to download from an app store. You add BistroTech to your home screen from your phone's browser, and from then on it opens without the browser bar. Open BistroTech in Chrome and sign in. On the Today tab, open the Set-up: … of … done marker. Under the Put it on your phone step you'll find the Add to your home screen card. Press its Install button. Confirm when the browser asks. If you've already hidden the set-up list, More has a Put it on your phone row too, for as long as the browser can install the app. If you don't see the button anywhere, you can install it from Chrome's menu instead. Open BistroTech in Safari and sign in. Open the Share menu. Choose Add to Home Screen, and confirm. In a new account, step 2 of the First steps guide shows this too on an iPhone or iPad in Safari, in a Put it on your phone part. You turn notifications on for this device on the Notifications page, under Notifications on this device (the switch is on My login too). After you do, we send a test to this device. If it arrives, you're done. If it doesn't, the app asks if you got it and explains what might be missing. On iPhone, you may need to add the app to your home screen. Browser permission or the phone's silent mode may also be the cause. You can request up to 6 tests a day. On iPhone, notifications only work from the BistroTech you added to your home screen. They go to the device you turned them on for, so you'll need to turn them on separately on each one. Read Alerts for more about notifications of low reviews. The icon may show how many replies are waiting for you, matching the Válaszok tab, where you find replies. The number disappears at zero. This may work on Android and in the iPhone home-screen app, but not in a browser tab. Notifications still arrive if your phone doesn't show the number. If you have several accounts, a notification puts its own account's count on the icon. Once you open the app, the count changes to the account you have open. If you have several accounts, the notification's title names the account. Tap it and that account opens, with a line at the top that says “Switched to” and the account's name. If the notification is about one review and a draft reply already exists, it takes you straight to the reply. Otherwise you land on the list of low reviews. On Android and desktop Chrome, a low-review notification has Megnyitom (open) and Válaszok (replies) buttons, and the morning report's notification has only Válaszok. iPhone doesn't show buttons. Tap the notification itself. A low-review notification vibrates; the morning report is silent. The notification includes the star rating, but not the review's text. Under Your devices, you can mute sounds on this device separately. Your login's sound setting stays as it is. You can keep it quiet in the restaurant and have sound in the office. On Android, pressing and holding the icon, and in desktop Chromium a right-click, may give you shortcuts to these pages, if the device supports them. Replies. Reviews. Add a venue. Review QR code (it opens the venues page). iPhone doesn't support this. In Android Chrome, sharing a Google Maps link may open Éttermek, the venues page. The link goes into the new-venue search. A short maps.app.goo.gl link can't be resolved, so add the place's name instead. Sharing a sentence may open Asszisztens, the assistant, with the sentence in the question field. It doesn't send the question. These options depend on the device; sharing into the app isn't available on iPhone. BistroTech's /app address opens the app and keeps the part of the link after the question mark. On Android, the link may open the installed app instead of the browser. This depends on the phone; opening links this way isn't available on iPhone yet. The Today screen stays where it was and shows when it last refreshed. The last known numbers show on Today. Review text isn't kept on the device. If you switch notifications off on this device, you have 8 seconds to use Undo, like the one after approving a reply. Hover over the bar or move keyboard focus onto it to pause the countdown. The U key also undoes the action. If you close the page while the bar is there, the action goes ahead.

t: Searching help and using the question mark
s: Search help or use the question mark to open guidance for the screen you're on.
h: Searching help The question mark beside a screen title
b: Search in Súgó, the help page, to find guidance or the setting you need. Search covers all 22 help sections, the settings rows and the website's help articles. Try “daily report” or “password”, for example. A settings result opens the settings page it belongs to. To search reviews, replies and other account data too, use search across the whole account. The ? beside a screen's title opens its help section as a sheet over the page. At the top there is a help search that shows the three best matches. Links in the sheet open the full help section and the relevant article on the website.

t: What the numbers in the daily report mean
s: What counts as a new review, what you see for each venue, and what the parts at the end of the report are for.
h: What counts as new How the analysis counts reviews For each venue At the end of the report The analysis The same numbers on the Today tab
b: The daily report comes in two messages. The first has the numbers. The second is the analysis, and it only comes on days with reviews that have text. A review is new if the guest posted it since the previous morning report. Two reports never count the same review. If a report is made again, it gives the same number. If a guest rewrites their review, we don't count it again. The change shows in a separate part, as Changed and removed reviews explains. Kimutatások, the analysis tab, counts reviews by the date Google gives them. Ma, the morning screen, counts by the days of the morning reports, so the two views can differ by a few reviews. The ? on the tiles and table explains the number and the days it covers in the account's time zone. It also shows the last check, what counts towards the figure and why it can differ from Google's public total. A review removed by Google stays in the historical counts but leaves Válaszra vár, the count waiting for a reply. Tripadvisor reviews are kept out of the Google numbers here too. The public Google rating is cumulative. The period's average uses only that period's new reviews, so read them as separate figures. Themes and comparing your venues explains the views. How many new reviews came in, and their average. The star breakdown, from 5 down to 1. The venue's Google rating and its total number of reviews. A red mark if a one-star or two-star review came in. Venues with no new reviews get one line each at the end of the list. Under them, the “Total” line has the numbers for the whole account. “Unanswered negatives”: reviews of 3 stars or fewer, no more than 14 days old, that have been waiting at least a day and don't have a reply we can see yet. The oldest comes first, and each one links to the review. “No fresh data”: venues where the download failed or was skipped. The next successful download catches up on them. If none of your venues got a new review, the report may show an account-wide warning. Quiet-venue lines can replace it. The extra report lines explains the conditions. A day without a review is common for a smaller venue and doesn't mean anything's wrong. If you've connected Tripadvisor, a separate line shows the new reviews there. They're kept out of the Google numbers. The second message is built from the day's reviews with text. “Mentions by name” lists the staff members guests named. “Themes” shows what came up more than once. If there were no reviews with text that day, you won't get this message. The Today tab opens on the morning report's numbers and counts the same reviews. To see another period, use the Other period button. You can pick Report, Today (what's come in since the morning report), 7 days or 30 days (the last 7 or 30 morning reports). The stars for each venue are in the Full breakdown by star table, under Your venues, worst first. On a phone, open it first.

t: The extra report lines and the monthly summary
s: Separate switches for lines and links in the daily report and weekly summary, plus the monthly summary.
h: Where to switch them The original signals and the monthly summary Links and further signals Links in the report What doubled this week When a venue is quiet When the Google rating falls How long replies have waited Further lines in the weekly summary The report's name In the weekly summary
b: The daily report and weekly summary have extra lines and links to help you find what needs attention. Signals only appear when there's something to say. Open the Notifications and reports page of Settings and find the Report card. Switch on or off what you want. Each switch is saved at once, and Saved appears next to it. The account owner sets the switches. Negatives waiting for a reply, per venue: under each venue's line, you'll see how many 1-, 2- and 3-star reviews are still waiting for a reply, and how long the oldest one has waited. We only count the ones that came in after we started watching the venue. Time of day line: if at least 3 negative reviews came in that day, and most of them fall in the same part of the day, the report tells you which. It's lunch, afternoon, evening or night. What counts is when the guest wrote the review, not when they visited your venue. Review count drop: if the review count Google shows has dropped by 2 or more since the last reading, the report says by how much. We don't flag a drop of 1, because that's just Google's own churn. Monthly summary to the group: on the first of each month, a short piece about the month before. We send it to the same Telegram chat as the daily report. If you haven't connected Telegram, you won't get a monthly summary either. The daily report and weekly summary show the lines below when there's something to show. In the daily report and weekly summary, a venue's name opens its reviews for that report in the app. Válaszra vár, meaning waiting for a reply, opens the unanswered negatives. The total opens the day's reviews. The weekly summary's Teendők lines, for things to do, open the venue or reviews they name. In the daily report, on the first of each month, a line opens the previous month's printable summary. The daily report can flag a complaint theme at one venue when it has at least 5 mentions this week and reaches at least twice its own weekly average over the previous 8 weeks. It can flag a dish with 3 negative mentions this week. Up to 3 themes and 3 dishes appear. The comparison uses the venue's own data. Under a venue, the daily report can show how many days have passed without a review and the usual gap between reviews. This needs at least 1 week and at least 3 times the usual gap without a new review. The line also needs a review-count check from the report day or the day before. When there are venue-level signals, they replace Gyanúsan üres nap, the account-wide warning about a suspiciously empty day. When there are no such signals, the account-wide line stays. The daily report flags a venue whose public Google rating fell by at least 0.1 over the last 7 days. The line shows the earlier value and the value at the latest check. A separate daily report line shows how many replies are waiting and since when. The weekly summary can have a line about the actions behind replies and one about a filed case without an answer. On the same card, you can give the report a name in The report's name field. It goes at the top of the daily report and the weekly summary, in capitals. If you leave it empty, it says BistroTech. Press the Save button under the field to keep the name. The weekly summary's Teendők list, for things to do, draws partly on negatives waiting for a reply, the time-of-day signal and the review-count-drop signal. If one of these is left out of the report, it's left out of the weekly list. Read more in The weekly summary.

s: Every Monday you get the week that's just ended, venue by venue, compared with the week before.
h: Which week What is in it The weekly rank summary
b: On Mondays, the weekly summary comes shortly after the daily report. It goes wherever the daily report goes: to Telegram, or to the Sent messages page if no chat is connected. Owners can turn on A heti összefoglaló jöjjön hang nélkül, which makes the weekly summary silent. It's under A csoport szokásai, the group's habits, on Értesítések, the notifications page. The Monday message won't buzz. If only the operator can change the group's habits, the page tells you. Read Alerts for the other group settings. The summary covers the last 7 days, up to and including yesterday, and compares every number with the 7 days before that. For each venue, the number of new reviews, and which way that's moved since the week before. For each venue, how many 5-, 2- and 1-star reviews came in, and the weekly average. The totals for the whole account. The names mentioned most, venue by venue. The themes that kept coming up during the week. The breakdown of your guests' review languages, when we know the language of enough reviews. The “This week” list, with up to 3 things to do. If there's no data for part of the week, the heading tells you how many days of data went into the summary. If you're watching search phrases in the Rank view of the Analysis tab, there's a second summary on Mondays, about your positions on Google Maps. It goes to the Marketing destination on Telegram, but only if you've connected it. Your rank on Google Maps and your competitors has the details. You can read both summaries again on the Sent messages page, under the Weekly summary kind.

s: When we send alerts outside the daily report, and where they go.
h: Instant alert on a low review When the last message went out A test message on Telegram Separate quiet hours for your phone and Telegram Pausing a venue's alerts The Telegram group's habits By mail Pattern alarm Error message
b: Besides the daily report, we send three kinds of alert to Telegram. All three go to the Alerts destination, so it's worth connecting that one too, on Értesítések, the notifications page. It works the same way as for the daily report. On the same page, find the Instant alert on a low review card. In the Alert when the review is at most field, choose the number of stars. If you don't want the alert, choose Off. Under Csendes órák, meaning quiet hours, set when we should keep quiet. Every choice is saved at once, and Saved appears next to it. A new account starts at 2 stars. Once a review like that reaches us, we'll let you know within 15 minutes. Anything that comes in during quiet hours, we send together when they're over. If the Alerts destination isn't connected, this alert goes to the daily report's chat instead. If that isn't connected either, we've no way to tell you. On the Notifications page, under the morning report, the weekly summary and the alert, you see the last delivery. The line says when it went, on which channel, and whether it arrived. If the quiet hours held an alert back, it says so, and the Quiet hours section shows how many alerts are waiting and when they'll come. If sending failed, the reason is there. Owners also see the last message's state for the account's chats. Under your own Telegram chat, the Küldök próbaüzenetet button (send a test message) asks for a test. Owners also have the button under the account's chats. BistroTech replies with one line. You can request up to 5 tests an hour per login. Under Quiet hours for your devices, the Use different quiet hours on my devices switch lets you set another period for your phone. The phone can stay quiet at night while you still get the alert on Telegram, or the other way round. This section appears when the alert is on and you're not just a viewer. If you leave it off, the same quiet hours apply to both. Under Which venues, in the Pause one venue block, pick the venue from Which venue and choose how long: 1, 7 or 30 days, or until a day you pick. Then press the pause button. The Mégis szóljon button (alert me after all) turns it back on. This only pauses your own alerts. Until then we won't tell you about the venue's low reviews. The account's channel still gets them, and they're still in Replies. If the pause would leave nobody to get the venue's alerts, the Te vagy az utolsó panel (you're the last one) opens, the same as when you switch them off. Owners can change these settings under A csoport szokásai (the group's habits). The first switch limits questions to account members: the chat answers only people on the account. BistroTech recognises them through their own linked Telegram chats. Short answers in the chat: when it's on, the answer is cut to 600 characters, with a line under it that opens the app. Send the weekly summary without a sound makes the weekly summary silent. The Monday message won't buzz. For some accounts only the operator can change these settings, and the page says so. Read BistroTech on Telegram for its commands and the buttons under its messages. While email sending hasn't started, Hamarosan (coming soon) sits next to E-mail. We aren't sending letters yet. During the day, we watch for two patterns at each venue. One is several one-star reviews coming in over a short time. The other is several guests lowering an earlier rating within a few days. We only look at Google reviews for this. We'll tell you about the same pattern once a day, and once more that day if the count reaches twice the threshold. This alert only goes to the Alerts destination. It can also name who needs to be told. You set that person on the same page, in the Who to notify on an alert field, and keep it with the Save button under the field. If a venue has had several one-star reviews in the past 24 hours, a warning card shows up on the Today tab too. If the pattern looks suspicious, open a case for it, as Disputing reviews with Google explains. If something goes wrong on our side, like a venue's download, the Alerts destination gets a short message. Usually you don't need to do anything, because the next scheduled run catches up. Tip: Your phone can tell you about a low review too. Putting it on your phone shows you how.

s: Check today's numbers, take a reply, or quieten the group's alerts for a while.
h: Your own chat Commands Quiet for a while The buttons under an alert When someone has replied The group's settings
b: You can write to BistroTech on Telegram. /help tells you what the chat is for and which account it belongs to. Setting up the daily report explains how to connect it. In a group, BistroTech recognises you through your own linked chat. Connect it under Your own Telegram chat on the Notifications page. Without it, the buttons under a message ask you to connect your chat first, so that it knows who you are. You can type the commands. In your own chat with BistroTech, the / menu also lists them in the chat's language. Groups don't get that menu. /help tells you what the chat is for and which account it belongs to. /ma shows the number of reviews since the morning report, their average star rating and the lowest venue. /var tells you how many replies are waiting and which is the oldest. /kerdes is also listed in the menu. /csend works in the account's chats, for owners and for members who can see every venue, once they've connected their own chat. It doesn't work in your personal chat. /csend 2 óra holds the chat's alerts for 2 hours. /csend 30 perc holds them for 30 minutes. /csend ma requests quiet for the rest of the day. /csend vége ends the quiet period. A quiet period can last up to 24 hours. Afterwards, the chat receives everything that came in as one message. An alert about a 1- or 2-star review has these buttons. Open: the venue's name opens the reply in the app. If there's no draft yet, the button says Open in the app and opens the review. I'll take it marks the reply as yours for 10 minutes. Your name appears in the queue. Copy the reply sends the draft's text to your own chat with BistroTech so you can read and copy it. You can use this if you're allowed to reply for that venue. Not today pauses that venue's alerts for you until the end of the day, for at least 1 hour. The last three buttons appear only when the message is about 5 reviews or fewer. Nothing under the message approves or posts a reply. That isn't available from Telegram yet. You approve the reply in the app. When the reply to an alerted review is approved or posted, the message gains a line underneath within 15 minutes, saying who approved the reply and when. If someone replied on Google, the line says a reply went out on Google, with the time. A message covering several reviews changes once, when all of them have been answered. The owner can restrict questions to account members, keep answers in the group short and make the weekly summary silent. For some accounts, only the operator can change these settings. The app tells you when that's the case. Read Alerts for these settings and quiet hours.

s: How to find every review of one venue, one star rating or one word.
h: Search Searching the whole account Quick filters More filters Saved views Keys for reviews A review's card Notes and who handles it
b: The Reviews tab shows every review we've downloaded, newest first. At the top there's a search field and a few quick filters, on a phone too. The Filters button opens the rest. Type a word in the Search the reviews field, for example “goulash” or “waiter”, and we'll look for it in the text of your reviews. Accents don't matter, so “gulyas” finds “gulyás” too. Ctrl + K, or Cmd + K on a Mac, opens search across the account. You can also use Keresés (search) in the left-hand rail on a computer, or the Keresés row under Több (more) on a phone. Search venues, review text and guest names, as well as sent replies, reply drafts, notes and help. Results from Napló, the account's activity log, are visible to owners and members with access to every venue. You'll only see what your role and venue access allow. Accents don't matter, so “gulyas” finds “gulyásleves”. Each result shows its type and opens the relevant screen. Results can be reviews, replies, notes, venues, activity entries, help sections, settings and articles. The same box lists every destination under Ugrás, meaning go to. If you have at least 2 accounts, you'll also see Fiókváltás, for switching accounts. There's a separate article about search within help. All: takes every filter off. Needs a reply: reviews we've written a reply for, where the reply is still waiting for approval. 1 and 2 stars: the worst reviews. 5 stars: the best ones. Assigned to me: the ones you've been made responsible for. It only shows when there are some. The Filters button opens a panel. That's where you pick a venue (Venue, if the account has several) and choose between Google and Tripadvisor (Site, if you've connected Tripadvisor). You can filter by stars, period, reply, text and sentiment, and set the order (Newest first or Lowest rating first). The button at the bottom of the panel already shows the number of matches, for example “Show 12 matches”. Every filter that's on shows as its own label above the list. Take one off with its x, or all of them with All off. Tip: Your filters are kept in the browser's address bar too. Copy the address and send it to a colleague, and they'll open the same list. Set your filters, choose Mentés nézetként (save as a view) and give the view a name. You can save up to 8 views. Saved views appear above the list. Apply one with a tap, or remove it with its x. Your views are saved separately for each person and each account. Single-letter commands are on by default. On the Appearance page of Settings, under Keyboard shortcuts, the Single-key shortcuts (Replies, Reviews, jumps with g) switch turns them off. The switch applies only to the device where you change it. J and K move between rows. O opens the review on Google. N opens its notes. Enter opens Átnézem, the review action for a reply awaiting approval. ? shows the list of keys. The switch controls single-letter commands on Válaszok (replies) and Értékelések (reviews), as well as go-to shortcuts starting with g. Ctrl + K, or Cmd + K on a Mac, still works when it's switched off. With the switch on, go-to shortcuts work everywhere. Press g, then the destination's letter. m opens Ma, the today page. e opens Értékelések, the reviews page. v opens Válaszok, the replies page. k opens Kimutatások, the reports page. b opens Beállítások, the settings page. s opens Súgó, the help page. f opens Fiókom, your login page. The stars, the guest's name, the time and the language. The analysis, meaning the sentiment, up to 2 themes and the staff named. A New mark if it came in since your last visit. Whether it has a reply yet, and a link that opens the review on Google or on Tripadvisor. The Notes, assignee link under the review opens the team's own part. In the Assigned to field, you choose which colleague handles it. Under Internal notes, you write what you know about the case, and save it with the Add button. Only your team sees the notes, never the guest. Colleagues with the viewer role can only read them.

s: What happens when a guest rewrites a review, or when Google takes one down?
h: If the guest rewrites it If an approved reply hasn't gone out If the reply is already posted If Google takes a review down
b: A review can still change after it's posted. The guest can rewrite it, or Google can take it down. We keep an eye out for both. On Google, a guest can leave one review per venue. When they rewrite it, Google sometimes gives it a new ID. To us it's still the same review, and we don't count it twice. The Reviews tab always shows you the latest version. We keep the old version too, so you can see what changed. The “Changed reviews” part of the daily report shows what changed from what, like 5 stars down to 1, or just the text. Reviews that went down come first, with their new text. The change isn't counted again in the report's numbers. If the guest changes the review text or stars, the reply returns to the queue. The rating doesn't have to fall for this to happen. Read it again and approve it again if it's still right. Nothing goes out until you do. If a guest lowers a review we've already answered by 2 or more stars, or rewrites its text without raising the stars, the reply comes back to the Replies tab. The card says The guest changed their review, with how many stars it was and is now, or that only the text changed. It also shows the Earlier text and the reply that's on Google right now. For a 1, 2 or 3 star review we write a new reply, and until it's ready the old words sit in the editor. Approve the new one and it replaces the old one on Google, within a quarter of an hour where we're the manager. No reply leaves the old reply up. If the stars rose or fell by only 1, and the text is the same, the review stays answered. We keep the old reply too, and Activity records both the return and the replacement. We don't follow reviews the guest deleted and posted again this way. If you edited the reply on Google yourself, we don't replace it. You decide. If several guests lower their rating at one venue within a few days, we'll send you a pattern alarm. More in Alerts. Tip: You can also ask the Assistant page which reviews changed in a given period. Google sometimes removes reviews, for example when one breaks its rules. We can tell because the review count on your Business Profile goes down. If the count has dropped by 2 or more since the last reading, the daily report's “Google removal” line tells you. A drop of 1 we don't flag, because that's just Google's own churn. The count alone can't tell us exactly which review has gone. You can turn the line on or off on the Report card, on the Notifications and reports page of Settings. The details are in The extra report lines and the monthly summary. If the drop looks suspicious to you, open a case for it on the Disputes page. Disputing reviews with Google shows you how.

s: If your venue's on Tripadvisor, we bring in its reviews from there too, kept apart from the Google numbers.
h: Switching it on What changes then If something goes wrong Switching it off
b: You turn Tripadvisor on one venue at a time, and it's the account owner who can do it. Open the venue's page on Tripadvisor and copy its address from your browser's address bar. It starts like this: “tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-”. In BistroTech, open the Venues page, click the venue's row, and open its Setup tab. On the Tripadvisor card, paste the address into the The venue's Tripadvisor address field. Press the Connect button. The first download takes a few minutes and brings in up to 150 reviews from the last 6 months. The card updates itself in the meantime. After that, we refresh once a day, before the morning report. On the venue page, Hol van kint a hely, the list of sites where your venue appears, shows olvassuk, meaning we read it, next to Tripadvisor as long as Tripadvisor is switched on. On the Reviews tab, Tripadvisor reviews have their own mark. Use the Site row of the Filters panel to show only those, or only the Google ones. In the daily report, new Tripadvisor reviews get their own line. They don't get mixed into the Google numbers. We write replies to these too. We can't post to Tripadvisor, though, so you copy the reply and post it from your Tripadvisor owner account. Posting a reply by hand, without Google access shows you how. Auto-answer never posts a reply to a Tripadvisor review on its own. If the download fails, the card tells you why, and we try again the next morning. If the address isn't a Tripadvisor restaurant page, the card says so and nothing changes. Use the Switch off button on the card. The reviews you already have stay, but no new ones come in.

s: Make a short link and a QR code that guests can use to write you a review on Google.
h: Making a link Sharing from your phone What the count tells you What the guest sees The rules the link keeps The link's name and state Switching off and deleting
b: You can make a short link with a QR code for any of your venues. Whoever opens it sees the venue's name and a button for writing a review on Google. If you've connected Tripadvisor too, they can write one there as well. The account owner and members can make links. Open the Venues page, click the venue's row, and open its Setup tab. On the Ask for reviews card, type where the link will go, for example “table card”. Only you see this, not the guest. Press the New link button. The Copy link button copies it, and you can send it in a message. Use Megosztom, meaning share, to share an active link. The message thanks the guest for visiting, politely asks them to write a few words on Google and includes the link. You can edit it before sending. If your phone has no share sheet, the Copy the text button copies it. Share the same link with every guest, without conditions or rewards. The card shows how many times the link was opened in the last 30 days, and next to that, the number of Google reviews over the same period. The two may move together, but that doesn't mean one causes the other. Google doesn't tell us who wrote a review through the card. The guest sees a short page that thanks them for coming and asks them to say how it was. It's in their phone's language if that's Hungarian, English, German, French, Italian or Spanish, and in English for anything else. Apart from the language, every guest sees the same thing. The page and the printable card address the guest politely. We ask everyone the same way. We don't ask first whether they were happy. We don't promise a discount, a gift or anything else in return. Google forbids incentives and may remove reviews because of them. We don't ask the guest to name anyone, and there are no per-waiter codes. You can rename each link. Its card shows Él (active) or Kikapcsolva (switched off). After Switch off, the link only shows a page saying it's no longer active. You can only delete a link once it's switched off, with the Delete button, and that also loses the count of opens.

s: Open a case on suspicious reviews and get a dated document to back up your report to Google.
h: When to open a case Opening a case The document Reporting a single review In Google's own tool If someone asks for money to take reviews down Appealing Afterwards
b: You'll find cases on Disputes. The account owner opens and changes cases. Several one-star reviews came in for a venue in a short time. Guests went back and lowered an earlier rating. Google took reviews off your venue's listing. You want to report a single review. Press the New case button. The last 14 days list shows our alerts and the days your review count fell. If one fits, Use this one fills in the form for you. If you know about something we didn't catch, fill in the Venue, What you're documenting, From this day and To this day fields yourself. Press the Open the case button. In the list of cases, open the case with the Open link. Open the document opens it in a new tab, where you can save it as a PDF using your browser's print option. If you'd rather have a text file, press Download as Markdown. The document has the venue and its Business Profile ID, the period, and the review count day by day. It compares the one-star reviews with the venue's previous 90 days, and quotes every review in the period word for word. At the end come the changed reviews, our alerts and Google's own pages, with the date we read them. The document doesn't claim the reviews are fake. Whether a review comes down is entirely Google's call. A case can hold a single review. On Reviews, in a review's details, the Bejelentem link (report it) takes you to Disputes, to the Report a review card. Choose a reason under What are you reporting it as?, then press Open the case. In the case, the Bejelentés a Google-nél section (reporting to Google) shows the steps and the paragraph. Spam, nem valódi aktivitás means spam or inauthentic activity. Nem a helyről szól means it's not about the venue. Összeférhetetlenség means a conflict of interest. Zaklatás means harassment. Gyűlöletbeszéd means hate speech. Személyes adat means personal information. Trágárság means profanity. Pénzt kérnek a levételéért means someone is asking for money to take it down. These are Google's policy headings. Once you've chosen a reason, A Google-nek szánt bekezdés, the paragraph for Google, appears. Use Másolom, meaning copy, to copy it. The paragraph brings together the period, the counts, the venue's usual one-star rate over the previous 90 days and repeated wording. It doesn't pass judgement on the reviews. If we couldn't read all the reviews of the period or of the previous 90 days, the counts say at least that many. The case lists these steps from Google's help. Open Google's Reviews Management Tool. Confirm the account, then choose the business. Choose Report a new review for removal. Choose Report next to the review, select the reason and send the report. Don't pay. Pénzt kérnek a levételéért, the reason for a demand for money, points to Google's separate form rather than the usual Reviews Management Tool. Have your contact details and your relationship to the business ready. The form asks for the business name, address, profile ID and Maps link, the period and number of the 1- and 2-star reviews, how and when the demand arrived and what was asked for. You'll also need screenshots and dates. If Google rejects the report, it allows 1 appeal. Under Appeal eligible reviews, you can select up to 10 reviews. Send the appeal in Google's own tool. The case's Fellebbezés section (appeal) shows for cases marked as filed, and it only records that you've done it. If you tick a review that's already in another case's appeal, saving gives an error. In the case's What Google said part, fill in the Status, Google case reference and Notes fields, then press Save. When you set it to filed, we note today's date. Your notes show on the document too. If 14 days have passed since filing with no change, the case and Ma, the Today page, show how many days it's been without a reply. Megnyitom a Google értékeléskezelőjét opens Google's Reviews Management Tool again. Once all the reviews named in a case have disappeared from Google, the case closes and shows a date beside the closure. Until then, it shows how many of the total have come down. If the case only names a period, it shows how many reviews from that period no longer appear. If lots of one-star reviews came in over a short time, review attack waves explains the alarm and the pause. BistroTech never files anything with Google. You send both the report and the appeal yourself, in Google's own tool.

s: When lots of one-star reviews arrive in a short time, you get an alarm and time to look through them.
h: When it starts What the Disputes page shows When it ends Why it helps to wait
b: If an unusually large number of one-star reviews appears at a venue in a short time, you get an alarm on Telegram or in the app. It goes to the alarm chat, not the group report. The alarm alone doesn't pass judgement on the reviews. The threshold follows the venue's own volume. A 6-hour period needs at least 3 one-star reviews, and at least 3 times the usual number of one-star reviews for a 6-hour period over the previous 90 days. The alarm tells you which threshold it used. It also says when several reviews use mostly the same words. At the top of Disputes, the line tagged as a wave shows how many one-star reviews arrived and over how many hours. The line asks you to wait before replying until it's clear what's happening. No reply goes out to Google for the wave's reviews while it lasts, whether automatic or approved. The rest wait in the queue. The wave doesn't affect the venue's other reviews. Open the case (and the Ügy nyitása link at the end of the alarm) fills in a new case form with the venue, the period and the wave's reviews. The form's own Open the case button then opens the case. If the wave already has a case, you see See the case instead. Only the account owner sees this. Disputing reviews with Google explains how to report them. The account owner can lift the pause with Feloldom (release it). After 48 quiet hours following the wave's last review, the pause lifts itself. One line goes to the alarm chat saying the wave has ended. It names the venue and gives the number of reviews we've seen come down from Google since then, along with the number still waiting for a reply. A quick apology under an attack review can make its claim look credible. The pause gives you time to look through the reviews and report them first. BistroTech never files anything with Google. You send the report yourself, in Google's own tool.

s: How to look over the finished replies and approve them.
h: Step by step Before you approve If there's no draft After approval When the card says this
b: We write a reply to every new review with text, and to every review rated 1 to 3 stars, whether or not it has text. We don't draft replies to reviews of 4 or 5 stars with no text unless you ask. You can narrow this down in Settings, for example to 1 to 3 stars only. By default, no reply goes out without your approval. If you turn on auto-answer (a separate add-on), replies to the reviews you've chosen can go out without it, and by default that's positive reviews only. Open the Replies tab. Next to the tab you can see how many replies are waiting. At the top you can narrow the queue to one venue or one star rating. The worst review comes first. Read it, and you'll find the reply underneath. If the review's in another language, there's a translation under it, and one under the reply too. Edit it if you need to. Open the Rewrite part under the reply first. The Rewrite buttons can make it shorter, warmer or firmer, or switch it to formal or informal address. There's a limit on how many rewrites you can ask for in an hour. You can always go back to the original. Press Approve. You can undo it for the next 8 seconds with the Undo button. On a phone the button sits at the bottom of the screen, in the Decision bar, next to No reply. Until you've read the reply to the end, it says To the reply and takes you to the start of the reply. Once you've read it to the end, the button says Approve, and you can also swipe right to approve, or left to close it without a reply. If you have added us as a manager on Google and we've accepted the invitation, we'll post the reply within 15 minutes. If not, copy it with the Copy and open Google button and paste it in on Google. Tip: Faster with a keyboard. A approves, S closes without a reply, J and K move, E edits, O opens Google, U undoes. It works on a computer. If you dictate or use a screen reader, switch them off on the Keyboard shortcuts card, on the Appearance page of Settings. Press No reply and we'll close the review without a reply. We ask once for a reason, but you can skip the question. Any reason you give stays in the history. You can still find the review later under Reviews. Use Vissza a sorba (back to the queue) in the history to bring back a review closed without a reply, with a short reason. This doesn't change replies already on Google. A posted reply can't be reopened. If you can't decide now, you can put the reply aside or hand it to a colleague. Több kijelölése (select several) lets you handle several waiting replies together. Bulk approval is deliberately unavailable. See Later, hand over and reminders for the details. Words banned in your reply rules can't go out by hand either. If a banned word is in the reply, we tell you at approval, and it can't be approved until you take it out. Unfinished edits stay on this device. If neither the review nor the draft has changed, your text goes back into the box. If either has changed, we offer your text without inserting it. Always read the reply again before approving. Under Reviews, I'll reply lets you reply to a review that has no draft. You write the reply yourself. If the guest changes the review text or stars before an approved reply goes out, the reply returns to the queue. Read it again and approve it again if it's still right. Nothing goes out until you do. When automatic answering is on, a reply approved automatically waits 30 minutes before posting. During that time you can take it back with Take it back to edit, under Approved, not yet posted on Replies, and it waits for you. If an approved reply couldn't go out, the didn't go out card on Today shows the reason and the next step. Tap a row to get to Replies, where you can post it to Google by hand. See Posting a reply by hand. In the history, under What happened next? on a posted reply, you can tick what you did about it (I talked to the team, I told the kitchen, We fixed it, Something else) and add a line. The queue refreshes by itself when you come back to the tab or the window, and after every approval, skip or undo. Today refreshes too when you come back. In English and The reply in English (or your account's language) show the translations for you. If a translation is folded away, tap its line. It's there for you only: the guest gets the original. “There's already a reply on Google, so you can only close it.”: someone replied to this review on Google in the meantime, so this reply isn't needed. Close it with No reply. “It's not on Google any more, so you can only close it.”: the guest or Google took the review down, so you can't reply to it. Close this one with No reply too. Sensitive review: it contains a threat, an accusation or a health claim. We wrote a short, neutral reply and won't post it on our own, even with automatic answering on. Read it before you decide: you can approve, rewrite or skip it as usual. If it's a threat or hate, report it to Google; Disputing reviews with Google shows how, and the card's How to report it link brings you there too. The guest changed their review: the guest lowered or rewrote a review that's already answered. Approve the new reply and it replaces the one on Google. More in Changed and removed reviews. If a colleague is working on the reply, you can only read it for now. The card shows when it's free for you to take over. As the owner you can decide anyway. A reply is yours for 10 minutes when you open it, and for longer while you type. Approving, closing or leaving lets it go. Under the review, you can also see who looked at the reply and who took it. Only people who can reply are listed. When a review is already answered on Google or no longer on Google, we also close its reply ourselves as soon as we notice.

s: How to make the replies sound like you, with the rewrite buttons, the voice notes, the rules and the sign-off.
h: The rewrite buttons The voice The rules What applies at a venue Facts and saved sentences What we keep to in suggested replies
b: We write the replies to your settings, always in the guest's language, or in the account's language if the guest only left stars. We don't draft replies to 4- and 5-star reviews with no text unless you ask. I'll reply lets you write a reply to those yourself. On the Replies tab, open the Rewrite part under the reply. You'll find 5 buttons there: Shorter, Warmer, Firmer, Formal and Informal. Each press is one rewrite, and the new text replaces the old one. The Back to the previous text link brings back the text from before the rewrite. The Restore original link brings back the first version we wrote. A rewritten reply still only goes out when you approve it. If you ask for lots of rewrites within an hour, rewriting pauses for a while. You can still edit the text yourself in the meantime. On Beállítások (Settings), under Válaszok (Replies), you can set the form of address, sign-offs and length. You can add up to 3 sample replies, written as you'd write them. You can ask for a sample before saving. The voice you save applies from the next review. With a new account, you can also set it up during the first import. While you do that, we pause reply writing for up to 10 minutes so the first replies sound like you too. You can give a single venue its own notes too. On the Venues page, click the venue's row, open its Setup tab, and write them on the Voice notes card. On the same page, the Reply rules card holds a few firm rules. A choice saves as soon as you make it. Where you type text, press the Save button under the field. Form of address: As the guest wrote (formal when unclear), Always formal or Always informal. You can set separate Hungarian, English and German sign-offs. The reply ends in the guest's language. If there's no sign-off for that language, it ends with the venue's name. Under Never write, enter banned words separated by commas. We catch other forms of the words too. If a reply would still contain one of them, that reply isn't made. You can't post it by hand either: we tell you at approval, and it can't be approved until you take it out. At most this many words: by default 70 words for a positive review, 120 for a negative one. The rules apply from the next review on, and we don't rewrite replies that are already written. The account owner sets the voice and the rules. What applies here, on the Replies page of Settings under the rules and on the venue's Setup tab, brings together the account's voice, the rules, the venue's notes, the sign-off and the facts. They're shown in the order used to write the reply. On Venues, under Setup, an owner can add up to 12 facts for replies to quote word for word. These might cover the address, opening hours, parking, allergens or where lost property is kept. Replies may quote these exactly and won't invent other details about them. After 90 days, we ask whether they're still true. Until you confirm them, they won't appear in replies. You can also save up to 5 frequently used sentences here. A suggested reply may use them when they fit the review. We never promise a refund, a discount, free food or any other compensation. We never put a phone number, an email address or a link in a reply. On a negative review we apologise once. We don't argue, and we don't blame the guest.

s: Put a reply aside, hand it to a colleague or set a reminder to come back to it.
h: Put a reply aside Hand it over Handle several replies together Your inbox Set a reminder Evening summary When a low-rated review stays unanswered
b: You don't have to decide on every reply straight away. You can put it aside, hand it to a colleague or set a reminder. On a waiting reply, Később (later) lets you put it aside until tonight, tomorrow morning, after the weekend or a date you choose, whichever still fits. You can add a note too, such as saying you're waiting for the shift manager. The reply leaves the list but still counts among the waiting replies. Halasztott (put aside) shows those you've set aside. When it's due back, it returns to the top with the visszajött (returned) tag, and you get a message. You can put aside a reply to a 1- or 2-star review for no more than 3 days. Putting a reply aside doesn't answer or close anything. Use Átadom (hand over) to pass a reply to a colleague who can see the venue. Add a line for them. Your colleague gets a push or Telegram message and finds the reply under Rám vár (waiting for me). It also stays in the shared queue. Több kijelölése (select several) lets you select several waiting replies. You can close them without replying, hand them to a colleague or add the same note to all of them. Bulk approval is deliberately unavailable. Régi vázlatok lezárása (close old drafts) closes the drafts older than 7, 14, 30 or 60 days for all venues or one you pick. You can narrow it by star rating too. Sensitive reviews and replies put aside are excluded. You can undo this closure once, within 30 minutes. Napló (activity log) shows the number of drafts closed in one entry. The bell opens Jelzéseid (your notifications). It also shows messages that didn't reach you through any channel. A reply handed to you or returned to the queue. A reminder or evening summary. An overdue complaint. A held sensitive review. A venue whose alerts reach nobody. Use Emlékeztess (remind me) on a review, reply or venue. Pick tomorrow, in a week or a date. You'll get the reminder in the app and on your own channel. While it's open, it also appears on the Today screen. You can turn on Esti összefoglaló (evening summary) under Értesítések (notifications). It's off by default. You get one line at the hour you choose, only when something is waiting. It isn't sent during your quiet hours. Owners can turn on the 24- and 48-hour reminders under Értesítések (notifications). They're off by default. If a 1- or 2-star review still has no answer after 24 hours, the people covering the venue get a reminder. After 48 hours, every owner does. You choose the hours. Each person gets one message, never in the group chat. Two other messages to owners are also off by default. One flags a venue whose alerts reach nobody. The other flags a sensitive review that's been held.

s: Switch it on, and replies to good reviews can go out without your approval. You have 30 minutes to stop them first.
h: Turning it on What it means Turn it off for one venue If you extend it to lower reviews Turning it off In the subscription
b: By default, a reply only goes out once you've approved it. Automatic answering takes that over from you, from a star rating you choose upwards. It starts switched off, and only the account owner can turn it on. Open the Replies page of Settings and find the Automatic answering card. Turn on the Automatic answering on switch. Under Which good reviews we answer ourselves, pick 4 and 5 stars or 5 stars. By default it's 4 and 5 stars. There's nothing to save: every choice is saved as soon as you make it, and Saved appears next to it. Replies to reviews at or above the stars you set don't wait for your approval. They wait 30 minutes before posting. During that time, Take it back to edit, under Approved, not yet posted on Replies, takes a reply back, and it waits for you. If you don't stop it, it can go out without anyone reading it first. 4- and 5-star reviews with no text don't get a reply, so nothing goes out to them automatically either. Replies to lower reviews still wait for you on the Replies tab. Replies posted this way are marked “automatic” in the list and in the history. It only covers Google reviews. Replies to Tripadvisor reviews always wait for your approval. A review marked Sensitive review (a threat, an accusation or a health claim) never gets an automatic reply. It waits for you on the Replies tab. It only works if the Reply writing on switch, on the Reply writing card of the same page, is on as well. We can only post the reply where you've added us as a manager on your Google Business Profile and we've accepted the invitation. Anywhere else the reply's still written, but you'll need to paste it in yourself (see Adding us as a manager on Google). If the guest changes the review text or stars before posting, the approved reply returns to the queue. Read it again. Nothing goes out until you approve it again. When automatic answering is on for the account, you can turn it off for an individual venue on Éttermek (Venues), under Beállítás (Setup). Every reply at that venue then waits for you. Warning: If you turn on We answer 1–3 star reviews ourselves too, in the Bad reviews part of the card, replies to lower reviews can also go out without anyone reading them first. You can stop these during the 30-minute wait too. They appear on your own Google Business Profile, where your guests see them. The page says this above the switch too, and asks once more before it turns on. Only Yes, switch it on starts it. We then answer 3-star reviews first. Under Which ones get an automatic reply? you can go lower (2 and 3 stars, All of them, 1 star too), and we ask again at each step. While this is on, we answer the 4 and 5 star reviews too. A bad reply to a negative review is public. It's worth seeing how your replies sound first, by approving them yourself. Rewriting and the reply rules can help with that. Turn off the Automatic answering on switch. That's saved at once too. Replies that have already gone out stay on Google, but every new reply waits for your approval again. The Activity page records it whenever it's turned on or off. On the Subscription page, you'll find it among the add-ons as Auto-answer. Its price hasn't been announced yet.

t: Posting a reply by hand, without Google access
s: If you haven't added us as a manager, you copy the finished reply with one button and paste it in on Google yourself.
h: Step by step If an approved reply couldn't go out If you have no time now For a Tripadvisor review Worth knowing
b: Without manager access to a venue's Google Business Profile, we can't post the reply for you. We still write it, and you still approve it. The only difference is that you paste it in. If a review has no draft, I'll reply under Reviews lets you write the reply yourself. This doesn't give us access to post it. Words banned in your reply rules can't go out by hand either. If a banned word is in the reply, we tell you at approval, and it can't be approved until you take it out. On the Replies tab, approve the reply with the Approve button. The reply is ready panel appears. Press the Copy and open Google button. The reply is copied to your clipboard, and the review opens on Google in a new tab. On Google, paste the text in as your reply and send it. Come back and press I've posted it on Google in the panel, which stays open until then. That closes the reply, the History shows “posted by hand” next to it, and from then on Today and the reports no longer count the review as unanswered. It can't be undone. If we don't have a link to the review, the panel shows the Copy reply button instead. You'll then need to find the review in your Google Business Profile yourself. If the reply came back because the guest changed their review, the panel also says “On Google, put it in place of the old reply.” Then close it with I've posted it on Google as usual. On Today, the didn't go out card lists approved replies that couldn't be posted, with the reason and the next step. Tap a row to get to Replies, where you can post it to Google by hand. The reason may be missing or removed Google access, a review that isn't on Google, a review that changed, or Google refusing the reply. If the guest changes the review text or stars before posting, the reply returns to the queue. Read it again and approve it again if it's still right. Nothing goes out until you do. Press the Later button. The reply waits for you on the Replies tab, in the Approved, not yet posted list, marked “post it by hand”. Pick it up from there whenever you like, with the Copy reply button and the Open on Google link. The I've posted it on Google button is there too, next to each of these replies. We can't post to Tripadvisor. You'll see the Copy and open Tripadvisor button there, and you post the reply from your Tripadvisor owner account. Tripadvisor replies don't have an I've posted it on Google button yet. If you forget to press I've posted it on Google, that's fine. We read the venue's reviews again every day, and if your reply is already under the review, we close the approved reply ourselves. We don't compare the words, so we can't tell whether it was our reply you posted. If Google removed a review in the meantime and the daily read no longer finds it among the last 2 days, its reply leaves the queue too. Reviews removed longer ago aren't found this way yet. If we lost manager access at a venue, the panel says so, and the row reads “we lost Google access, post it by hand”. You post the reply yourself the same way. If you'd rather not post replies by hand, add us as a manager. Here's how: Adding us as a manager on Google.

s: The Analysis tab shows what keeps coming up in what guests write, and how your venues compare side by side.
h: The main numbers What's usual for your account Per venue If you have one venue Themes Staff mentions Downloading and printing
b: The Kimutatások tab, for analysis, shows the numbers for a period, venue by venue. At the top, choose 7, 30 or 90 days, or one of the last 3 calendar months, listed by name. A full month compares with the month before. The current month compares with the same number of days of the previous month. The period control shows those dates. Your choice stays for the session. On the dishes and staff views, a selected month counts as 30 days. The tab counts by the date Google gives each review. Ma, the morning screen, counts by the days of the morning reports, so the two can differ by a few reviews. Read more about how the numbers are counted. At the top of the tab you also switch between its views: Overview, Dishes, Staff and Rank. What follows is about Overview. You'll see 5 tiles. Changes compare with the previous period, and the first 2 tiles also have a small day-by-day line. New reviews: the reviews that came in during the period. Average: the mean of the new reviews' stars. Negative: the new reviews of 1, 2 or 3 stars. Below it you see how many were serious, meaning 1 or 2 stars. Waiting for a reply: reviews whose reply we've written and nobody has looked at yet. It's the same number as on the Replies tab. Reply time. This shows the hours between a 1 to 3-star review and the owner's reply. You see the middle value, or median. Below it is the share of negative reviews answered, both compared with the previous period. Reply times for replies closed by hand are counted separately. A reply dated at or before its review, or more than 1 year later, is also left out of the median. You see a separate count of replies with uncertain times. Negative reviews written before the venue's first report are counted separately too. With fewer than 5 eligible replies, the tile says Kevés adat, meaning there is too little data. Below the tile, you also see the percentage of replies sent unchanged and how many replies that represents. Replies marked as posted by hand are left out of this figure. The first 3 tiles open the reviews behind them, and Waiting for a reply opens the Replies tab. If some of the period's reviews haven't been analysed yet, a note under the tiles tells you how many. Every tile and the table have a ?. Open it to read what the number means, which days it covers in the account's time zone, what counts towards it and when it was last checked. It also explains why the count can differ from Google's public total. Below the new and negative review counts and Reply time, you'll also see a comparison with your account's own previous 90 days. A separate note marks a difference of at least 20% above or below that level. With fewer than 30 reviews in those 90 days, the line says there's no usual figure yet. Other restaurants' data doesn't count towards it. The Éttermenként section, meaning per venue, gives each venue one row. For the selected period, it shows these figures. The new review count alongside the previous period's count. The average rating of the new reviews and its change. The share of 1- and 2-star reviews and its change. The breakdown by star alongside the previous period's breakdown. The share of negative reviews answered and the median reply time. The Google-értékelés (Google rating) column is the public, cumulative figure, with the Változás (change) column beside it. It's separate from the average of the period's new reviews. The line shows the last 30 days, or the last 90 for a 90-day period. It uses the venue's own scale, and the dot is today's value. A switched-off venue still appears if it had reviews in the period. Its name carries the Switched off tag, so a past period keeps the figures for the venues that were part of it. A line under a venue's name can show how many days have passed without a review and the usual gap between reviews. It appears after at least 1 week and at least 3 times the usual gap without a new review. The usual gap comes from the venue's own last 90 days, up to the end of the period, with at least 10 reviews. The venue whose rating dropped most comes first. On a computer, click a column heading to sort it another way. On a phone, venues appear as cards, with a sort control above them. The per-venue table and the Leginkább line, meaning where a theme comes up most, are hidden. Instead, the bars under Hetente, meaning weekly, show the weeks alongside the previous period. You'll also see the star breakdown, the Reply time tile and the lines comparing your figures with what's usual. We read the reviews with text to see what they're about, like the service, the wait or the prices. Under What guests write about you'll find two lists, What guests praise and What guests complain about. Each shows the 10 most common themes. For each theme you see how many of 100 reviews mentioned it, and how that changed since the period before. If a theme comes up far more at one venue than at the others, the “Most at …” line names it. If a theme came up fewer than 5 times, we say there's too little data instead of showing a change. A review counts towards a theme only once. A theme counts as a complaint when it comes up in a review with a negative tone, or in one rated 3 stars or fewer. It counts as praise when it comes up in a review with a positive tone, or in one rated 4 stars or more. Each theme also has a small line showing its rate per 100 reviews over the last 12 weeks.
