A week with fewer than 5 reviews leaves a gap. Each theme gets one consistent name, so you can compare themes across venues and languages. Staff guests mention by name shows the 6 staff members mentioned most, spelled the way guests wrote them. One name at one venue is one person. Each name shows how many mentions it had and what share of them was praise. Here a mention counts as praise when it's in a 4-star or 5-star review. The All, per venue link takes you to the Staff view, as Staff and name mentions explains. Use Download as spreadsheet at the per-venue table, either theme list or the people list to save the rows. They keep the order you see on screen, and the file name starts with your account's name. You'll also find these in Letöltés, the download menu at the top. As an owner, you can reach the daily numbers CSV, reviews CSV and JSON export here too. Their file names also start with your account's name. Read more about downloading your data. Printable summary puts the period on one A4 page. Each venue also has a Konyhai kártya link for a kitchen-board card. Printable summary explains what they contain and how to print them.

t: What guests write about each dish
s: The Dishes page shows which dishes guests mention at each venue, and in what kind of review.
h: The table Sorting Download As the guest wrote it If the table is empty
b: Dishes is one of the views of the Analysis tab; switch to it at the top of the tab. It shows, venue by venue, what guests mention by name from your menu. At the top, choose 7, 30 or 90 days. If you chose a month on the overview, this view shows the 30 days behind it. Your choice stays for the session. Each row is one dish at one venue. Click a row to open the reviews that name it. The Mentions column shows how many reviews named the dish. The Average is the star average of the reviews that named the dish. Against the venue's average shows how far that average sits above or below the venue's own average over the same days. +0.30 means guests who named the dish liked it more than the place as a whole. The 30 dishes mentioned most come first; the All … rows button brings up the rest. The Venue field narrows the list to one venue. On a computer, click a heading to sort the table. Sort by dish to bring each dish's venue rows together, so you can compare where it turns out better. If the same dish does very differently at 2 venues, it's worth a look in the kitchen. Use Download as spreadsheet to save the list to a file. The file name starts with your account's name. Dishes show up the way guests wrote them, in their own language. We don't translate them or match them to your menu, so “gulyás”, “goulash” and “gulasch” are 3 separate rows. We collect dishes from analysed reviews shortly after a review reaches us. We don't analyse older reviews, so a new account won't have many dishes on the list in its first few days.

s: Who guests mention by name, and how to fold different spellings of one person's name together.
h: The table Name spellings Download Where else you see the names
b: Staff is one of the views of the Analysis tab; switch to it at the top of the tab. It lists the names guests wrote in their reviews, venue by venue. At the top, choose 7, 30 or 90 days. If you chose a month on the overview, this view shows the 30 days behind it. Your choice stays for the session. Each venue gets its own card with the 3 names mentioned most. Next to each name you see how many reviews mentioned it, and what share of those were praise. Below them are one guest's own words about the first person. Click a name to open the reviews that mention that person at that venue. The whole list (… rows) opens under the cards. Mentions shows how many reviews named the person. The Positive and Negative columns show the mood of the whole review the name came up in, not of the sentence about the person. The Other column holds neutral reviews and ones we haven't analysed yet. Use this list to thank people for praise, not to appraise your staff. By default it's sorted by the number of mentions. The negative column is shown too. The Order buttons sort it by name or by venue instead, and the Venue field narrows it to one venue. Guests spell the same person's name in different ways. On the Name spellings card, you tell us which spelling means whom. Type the name in the The name to show in the list field, for example “Roland”. Type the spelling in the How guests write it field, for example “Roli”. Press the Add button. From then on, the list shows them as one row. The account owner manages the name spellings. In the whole list, Download as spreadsheet saves the list to a file, filtered and sorted as you see it on screen. The file name starts with your account's name. The daily report's analysis lists the staff who were mentioned, by name, and the weekly summary has the names mentioned most. A card on the Today tab can also let you know when someone's been praised several times this week. Its Staff button brings you here.

t: Your rank on Google Maps and your competitors
s: See where you come in the Maps results for a search, and how the restaurants nearby are doing.
h: The search phrase and the starting point Adding a phrase The table of positions Competitors The weekly rank summary
b: Rank is one of the views of the Analysis tab; switch to it at the top of the tab. The account owner adds search phrases and competitors. The search phrase is what a guest would type into Google Maps, for example “goulash budapest”. The starting point is the spot on the map we measure the search from. We need it because Google puts places near the person searching first. Press the New phrase button, or Add the first phrase if you have none yet. The New search phrase form opens. In the Search phrase field, type what a guest would search for. In the Name of the starting point field, give the point a name, for example “Deák tér”. Open Maps with the Open Google Maps to find coordinates link. Right-click the point a guest would search from (on a phone, press and hold it), and copy the two numbers. Paste them into the Latitude (lat) and Longitude (lng) fields. You can also paste both at once into the first field. Press the Add phrase button. We measure once every morning, so you'll see a new phrase's result after the next morning run. You can have up to 30 active phrases at a time. Under Watched phrases, each phrase gets its own card. A large number shows where the venue stands now, with the phrase, the venue and the change in words beside it, for example “3 places ahead of 30 days ago”. Below that, a line shows the last 30 days: when it goes up, you moved ahead. If the venue isn't in the top 20, we tell you. The card's Actions menu holds History, Edit, Switch off and Remove. History shows the earlier measurements. Switch off leaves the phrase out of the morning run, and its earlier data stays. The Competitors board is at the bottom of the Rank view. It puts your venue next to up to 5 places nearby, so you can see their rating, how many reviews they have, how many they've gained, and their positions in your search results. Press the Add a competitor button. The list shows the places that came up for your phrases in the last 30 days. Press the Add button next to the one you want to watch. Switch on Daily competitor watch. While the watch is off, we don't look anything up, and the board shows the earlier measurements. Once it's on, we check the rating and review count of the places you added every morning. The Remove button in the Actions column takes a place off the board, but its earlier measurements stay. On Mondays there's also a summary of your positions. It goes to the Marketing destination on Telegram, if you've connected it. There's more on this in The weekly summary.

s: The period's numbers on one A4 page, with a separate card for the kitchen wall.
h: What's on the page Kitchen-board card Printing or saving a PDF
b: Printable summary in Kimutatások, the analysis view, puts the period on one black-and-white A4 page. It can cover the whole account or one venue, for 1 week, 30 or 90 days, or a calendar month. The period's numbers and their changes. The venues, worst first. The 3 most praised and 3 most complained-about themes. Staff mentioned by name, if you've ticked Nevek is, meaning include names, on screen. Unanswered negative reviews. The period's best quote, without the guest's name. For a monthly summary, you'll also see the public Google rating and review count at the start and end of the month. These are cumulative Google figures, separate from the average of the period's new reviews. The page also shows the dishes mentioned most and the change in rank. A venue's Konyhai kártya link opens its kitchen-board card. It contains the venue's 3 most praised names and one guest's words. The kitchen-board card always shows the most praised names. On the A4 sheet, names appear only if the Nevek is (names too) box is ticked. Choose the period, then open Printable summary or the venue's Konyhai kártya link for its kitchen-board card. Use your browser's print option to print on paper or save as a PDF. You need to log in to open the page. There's no public link. Themes and comparing your venues explains the numbers you see on screen.

s: Ask about your own reviews and numbers, and the assistant shows you what it based the answer on.
h: Asking What it can do for you
b: The Assistant page is in the Your venues group of the left-hand rail, or under More on a phone. It answers from your own account's data: the reviews, the daily numbers, the replies written, the themes and the positions. If there's no data for something, it'll tell you. Press the New question button, or pick one of the suggested questions, for example “What happened this week?” Type the question and press the Send button. Enter sends it too, and Shift with Enter starts a new line. Above the answer you'll see the rows it worked from (reviews, daily numbers, names, themes), so you know where every number came from. You get a set number of questions a day, and the page shows how many you've used today. Conversations are kept, so you can pick up any of them again from the Conversations list. The assistant can approve or skip a reply, and post one you've already approved to Google. It only does that when you've asked it to in your own message. It uses your login, so it can't do anything you aren't allowed to do. It won't rewrite a reply's text. If you want to change it, do that on the Replies tab. It can write a suggestion for your listing, but it doesn't change anything on Google by itself. The suggestion waits for you on the Listing page, and you decide there. Tip: If guests or colleagues call one of your venues something else, add its old name or nickname on the Account and team page of Settings, in the What the assistant should know about your venues field. Then it'll still understand the question.

s: The Listing page shows what your Google Business Profile says about you, what's gone stale on it, and what we suggest.
h: What you see for each venue If Google shows the venue as closed Where the venue appears The suggestions Writing to Google
b: You'll find the Listing page in the Your venues group of the left-hand rail, or under More on a phone. It only works for restaurants where you've added us as a manager on your Google Business Profile. Adding us as a manager on Google shows you how. At the top there's a table, with the venues that need a look first. Its columns are Hours, Holiday hours, Description, Photos and Suggestions, and each cell says fine or take a look. Click a row to get to that venue's card, further down in the same order. The card shows: Last read: when we last read the listing. Hours: whether they're published. Special hours in 30 days, Description (how many characters it has), Photos and Open suggestions. Reviews mentioning hours: how many reviews brought up your opening hours in the past 30 days. We read every linked venue's listing every Sunday, early in the morning. The account owner can also use Adatlap beolvasása, meaning read the listing, to read it straight away, up to 20 times an hour per account. The suggestions update afterwards. If you reach the limit, try again later. After a listing read, Éttermek, the venues page, shows Closed, says Google or Temporarily closed for those venues. The Cases and waves card on Today lists them too. On the venue page, Hol van kint a hely, the list of sites where your venue appears, shows the sources. Google and Tripadvisor show olvassuk, meaning we read it, when we read their reviews. For Facebook, Wolt, foodora and Booking, the account owner sets tervezzük, meaning planned, kézzel, meaning manual, or nincs ott, meaning not listed. We don't read those sites yet. Suggestions come from the numbers we already hold. You'll get one when guests found the door locked while the listing said the venue was open. You'll also get one when a public holiday is coming up with no special hours set, when the description is short or old, or when there aren't many photos. And from the week's good reviews, we'll suggest a weekly post. The weekly post is the only one we write text for. For the rest, you see what the listing says now and what made us flag it. We won't guess your opening hours. The account owner decides with Approve or Drop it. Writing to Google isn't switched on yet. An approved suggestion stays put, and the card tells you it hasn't gone out. Nothing goes from this page to Google today.

s: Bring colleagues into your account with an invite link or by email, and choose their role and which venues they see as you go.
h: Invite link Another link, or a replacement Inviting by email address Pending invitations If they are already in the account Inviting a viewer Insider invitations
b: The account owner invites colleagues from the Team page. You'll find it in the Account group of the left-hand rail, or under More on a phone. The Invite button opens a panel that holds everything this article covers. In the Create an invite link part of the Invite panel, use the Role field to choose whether they'll be a Member, an Owner or a Viewer. Under Venues, decide what they'll see. All of them gives them every venue, including ones you add later. To give them just a few, untick All of them and tick the venues you want. Press the Create link button. Copy the link with the Copy link button. Do it now, because we can't show it to you again later. Send it to your colleague in a message. The link works for 7 days and can be used to join once. You'll only see the Venues part once the account has a venue. An owner always sees every venue, so there's nothing to choose for one. When your colleague opens the link, they'll see the account's name, their role and their venues. If they don't have a login yet, they sign up with the Sign up button and land straight in the account. If they already have one, they use I have an account, sign in, and they're in just as quickly. And if they open the link while already signed in, the Join account button is all it takes. Above the finished link, the card shows which role and venues it gives. Another link makes one more link with the same access, and the earlier one keeps working. That way you can invite several colleagues, each with their own link. Replace link stops the earlier link straight away and gives you a new one in its place. Use it if you sent the link to the wrong person. If you change the Role or the Venues after making the link, it disappears from the card but keeps working. You'll find it under Pending invitations, where you can revoke it. If your colleague already has a BistroTech login, you can invite them by email address too. In the Invite panel, open the Invite an email address part. Type their address in the Email address field and choose their role. For a member or a viewer, pick their venues under Venues, just as you would for a link. Press the Invite button under the field. Tell them to sign in. Next time they do, they'll be in the account, with the venues you chose. For anyone who doesn't have a login yet, send the invite link instead. Invitations nobody has used yet are at the bottom of the Invite panel, in the Pending invitations list, with the role, the venues and the expiry date. You can cancel any of them with the Revoke button. If you've deleted every venue an invitation names, the list shows “No venue left” next to it. Nobody can join with it any more, so revoke it and make a new one. If the person you're inviting is already on the account, the invitation won't change anything. Their role and venues stay as they are. You can change those on the Team page, as Roles and access per venue explains. A viewer can look but can't change anything. They see every venue, or only the ones you tick on the invitation. You can invite one by link or by email address. Just choose Viewer in the Role field. There's more about roles in Roles and access per venue. In an internal account, meaning one of the team's own accounts, the Create an invite link part has an Insiders checkbox. Whoever joins with a ticked link gets the role you chose and becomes an insider: they see every feature in every account they're on, and they can write to Zsomb directly. In Pending invitations, such a link is marked “insider”. Someone already on the account can use it too, and that spends the link's one use. On the invitation page your colleague reads: “This link also makes you an insider. You'll see every feature, and you can write to Zsomb directly.” A customer account doesn't show this checkbox. More in Insiders.

s: Who can see and do what in the account, and how to give a colleague access to just a few venues.
h: The three roles Changing a role Access per venue Removing and leaving Activity
b: Everyone on the account has a role. You manage roles and access on the Team page, in the Account group of the left-hand rail, or under More on a phone. Owner: sees and can do everything. Owners invite and remove people, add and switch off venues, change the settings, and pick the package. Member: sees every page and can work on replies, so they can approve, skip and rewrite them. They can't change the account settings. Viewer: sees everything, but can't change anything. When several of you work on the same queue, the app shows who's working on a reply and holds it for them for 10 minutes. The owner can always decide anyway. The owner changes someone's role on the Team page, in the Role column of that colleague's row. The last owner can't be removed, and their role can't be changed. If that's what you're after, make someone else an owner first. On the Team page, in the colleague's row, press the Edit link in the Venue column. Untick All of them, and tick the venues they're allowed to see. Press the Save button. Someone who doesn't see every venue only sees the reviews and replies for their own venues. They won't see the account's totals, the team or the account's activity entries. They can still see their own sign-ins on the Your sign-ins card of My login. The owner always sees every venue. You can also pick the venues on the invitation itself, so the colleague joins with just those from the start. See Inviting colleagues. The owner takes a colleague off the account with the Remove button in their row. From then on, that colleague can't get to the reviews. To leave the account, use the Leave this account link. An owner can invite you back later. The Activity page shows who did what in the account. You'll see replies, changes to the team and the venues, settings and invitations. Use the buttons at the top to filter, for example to the Replies or Team area. The My sign-ins filter on the activity page shows your own sign-ins, when and from which device. New devices, two-step sign-in being turned on or off, recovery codes and a new password appear here too. Only you see them. The activity page is for owners and members who can see every venue; everyone can see the same list on the Your sign-ins card of My login. As an owner, you can also download the account's activity log as a CSV from this page. A line about a reply or a review opens that reply or review. A line about a colleague opens Csapat, the team page, and a venue line opens the venue. If someone edits a reply before approving it, the entry says so. Javaslat (draft) and Végleges (final) show the original draft and the approved text one under the other. The log also records when someone pauses a venue's alerts, including how long the pause lasts. Changes to the group chat settings get their own entry too.

s: If you run several accounts, the Group page puts their numbers in one table and writes a weekly summary about them.
h: A new account Creating a group The account's consent What the group sees Weekly summary about the group Deleting a group
b: One account can hold several venues, and you don't need a group for that. A group is for when you've got several separate accounts, say one per company, and want to see them together. If you own an account, you can create another one. That way one login runs several accounts. Click the New account link. On a computer it's at the top of the left-hand rail, under the account's name; on a phone it's at the bottom of More. Fill in the Account name field, and check the Time zone and Language fields. Press the Create account button. The new account opens straight away, and it starts with a 14-day trial too. The First steps guide walks you through adding a venue. You switch between your accounts in the Account field, which appears once you've got 2 accounts. One email address can own up to 3 accounts. If you need more, write to us: the page says so then, with the Feedback button right under it. Open the Group page. It's in the Account group of the left-hand rail, or under More on a phone. On the New group card, fill in The group name field and press the Create the group button. In the Accounts part, choose the account from the Account to add list, and press the Add an account button. You can only add accounts you own. Each account decides for itself whether to share its summary, on the Group sharing card, on the Account and team page of its own Settings. The account owner picks Share it or Don't share. If an account doesn't share, the group sees nothing of it. In the Per account table, each account gets one row. It shows the new reviews, the average, the 1-star reviews, the Unanswered negatives, the changed reviews and changes in rank. You choose the period with the 7 days and 30 days buttons. A switched-off venue's past days count towards the selected period. The venue count still shows only active venues. The group only sees counts and averages. No reviews, no guest names and no replies. Every Monday morning there's a summary about the group too, with the most important things to do. If you fill in the Telegram chat id field on the Group settings card, we'll send it there. If you leave it empty, you can read it under Latest weekly summary. To find the chat's id, connect the same chat to one of the accounts, then look on the Notifications and reports page of that account's Settings. First take the accounts out of the group with the Remove it button. Then, on the Group settings card, press Delete the group, and then Delete it. Your accounts, venues and reviews aren't touched.

s: On the My login page you change your password and turn on two-step sign-in. You can sign out of your other devices there too.
h: Two-step sign-in Recovery codes Changing your password Forgotten password Signing out of other devices New devices and your sign-ins
b: The My login page is about your own login, not the venues' account. To open it on a computer, click your name at the foot of the left-hand rail and choose the My login row, with your email address beside it. On a phone, the same row is at the bottom of More. With this on, you'll need a 6-digit code as well as your password. The code comes from an authenticator app on your phone, such as Google Authenticator. So even if your password leaks, nobody can sign in to your account with it. On the Two-step sign-in card, press the Turn on button. Scan the code that appears with the authenticator app, or type the key in by hand. Type the app's 6-digit code and press the Check and turn on button. From then on, we'll ask for the code after your password when you sign in. If the code isn't accepted, check that your phone's clock is right. You turn it off with the Turn off button, which needs a fresh code too. Turning on two-step sign-in ends with 10 recovery codes. Helyreállító kódok, meaning recovery codes, are shown only then. You can't view them again later. Each code works once. Save them with Másolás (copy) or Letöltés (download), then press Megvan, elmentettem (I've saved them). The card shows how many codes you have left. Új kódok gives you a fresh set, after you enter a fresh code from your authenticator app. Without your phone, choose Nincs nálad a telefon? Használj helyreállító kódot. on the sign-in code screen. This offers a recovery code when you don't have your phone. Enter one of your saved codes there. Signing in with a recovery code turns off two-step sign-in. The screen tells you before you press the button and reminds you afterwards. Set it up again on Fiókom, your login page. If you have neither your phone nor a recovery code, write to us through Can't get in? on the sign-in page. On the Password card, type your current password in the Current password field. Type the new one in the New password and New password again fields. It must be at least 8 characters. If you want to sign out of your other devices too, tick the Also sign me out on other devices box. Press the Change password button. While email sending is switched off, choosing Forgot password makes the sign-in page say that we can't send password emails yet, so you can't get a new password this way. No email goes out in this state. If you're signed in on another device, you can set a new password on My login. The foot of the sign-in page also says how to write to us: “Write to us with the Feedback button. We'll reply to your email address.” Can't get in? opens the Write to us sheet without signing in. Enter your email address and your message. When email sending is on, Forgot password shows this: “We've got your request. If there's an account with that address, an email with a reset link goes out to it. If it doesn't arrive, check your spam folder or write to us.” It shows the same even if the address has no login. The email titled Új jelszó a BistroTechhez (a new password for BistroTech) has a link that works for 1 hour. It opens the New password screen, where you enter your new password. Show lets you see it as you type. For an expired or used link, the screen says: “This link has expired or was used already. Ask for a new one.” Send a new link asks for another. The Más eszközök card, meaning other devices, lists your signed-in devices, when they were last used and which one you're using now. Kiléptetés beside a device signs it out within 1 hour. Lost your phone, or left BistroTech open on a shared computer? Kijelentkezés minden más eszközről signs out all your other devices. These also sign out within 1 hour. You'll stay signed in on the device you're using now. If you sign in with a password from a device you haven't used for this login in the last 90 days, you get a notification in your own connected Telegram chat. With email sending switched on, you also get an email. There needs to be a recorded sign-in to compare it with. Your first sign-in after the release provides that starting point. The notification is headed Új belépés a BistroTech-fiókodba, meaning a new sign-in to your BistroTech login. Its link opens Fiókom, your login page, with Nem te voltál? Léptesd ki a többi eszközt, és adj új jelszót. This tells you to sign out your other devices and set a new password if the sign-in wasn't yours. Below the card, Belépéseid, meaning your sign-ins, shows the newest 10 entries about your sign-ins, new devices, two-step sign-in being turned on or off, recovery codes and password resets. Only you see them.

t: Downloading your data and deleting the account
s: How to download the account's data or your own, and how to delete a venue, the account or your login if you need to.
h: The account's data Your own data Deleting a venue Deleting the account Deleting your login
b: You can download the account's data and your own login data whenever you like. There are three things you can delete: a venue, the account, or your own login. The account owner downloads it from the Download the account's data card, on the Subscription and data page of Settings. All data (JSON): the venues, the reviews with their analysis, the replies and the settings, all in one file. Reviews as a spreadsheet (CSV): just the reviews, as a table. An account set to English separates the columns with commas, one set to Hungarian with semicolons, so Excel in the same language opens it straight away. On Analysis, the Download button also opens a sheet that offers daily numbers as a CSV, reviews as a CSV and the account's data as JSON. These downloads are also for owners only. Their file names start with your account's name. As an owner, you can also download the account's activity log as a CSV from Napló, the activity page. Downloads of the account's data, of the reviews and of the log itself appear in the log, with who downloaded them. Read more about the log in the article about roles and access. On the My login page, the Download my data button gets you your login's data. That's your email address, the day you signed up, your accounts and the date you accepted the terms. On the Venues page, click the venue's row and open its Setup tab. At the bottom, on the We're watching this venue card, open the Delete the venue part and type the venue's name. Press the Delete for good button, and confirm. That deletes every review, reply and statistic of the venue for good. If you only want a break, switch it off instead with the We're watching this venue switch on the same card, and nothing's lost. On the Subscription and data page of Settings, on the Delete the account card, type your password and the account's name. Press the Delete the account button, and confirm. We then mark the account for deletion. The daily report stops straight away, and the account disappears for everyone on the team. You've got 30 days to bring it back, from the Accounts awaiting deletion card on the My login page, with the Restore button. After that it's deleted for good. Warning: If you want to keep the account's data, download it first. Once it's deleted for good, we can't give it back. The Delete my login card on the My login page deletes only your own login, not the venues' account. If you're the only owner of an account, make someone else an owner first, or delete that account. Type your password, and type “DELETE” in the field. Press the Delete my login button, and confirm. Your login is deleted straight away and for good. Your name and email address do stay next to the Internal notes you wrote on reviews, and on the accounts' Activity page for 180 days. If you'd like those deleted too, call us or write to our registered address (it's at the bottom of the page).

s: Choose how BistroTech looks for you, and which language you see it in.
h: Where you set it Three steps, in order Light or dark In the Glass style only Motion and sounds Keyboard shortcuts The language
b: Everyone sets their own appearance, so your colleagues see theirs, not yours. Your choice is saved with your login, so it looks the same on your other devices. On the Appearance page of Settings. Changes show up straight away, and there's nothing to save. Style, meaning the shapes. Pop has thick outlines, hard shadows and blocks of colour. Glass puts frosted panels over a soft glow of colour. Classic is restrained, with fine lines on a paper-white background. Colours. You'll only see the colours of the style you picked. Pop has Lemon, Aperol, Matcha, Gelato, Balaton and the dark Midnight. Glass has Market, Aperol, Gelato, Balaton, Matcha, and the dark Neon and Paprika. Classic has Classic and Classic night. Font. Pick the typeface for headings and numbers from the style's own set. Body text uses the same face in every style. By default, you'll see Pop with automatic colours and Space Grotesk. Pick Light, Dark or Automatic. Automatic stays light by day and switches to the night colours after dark, as your device does. So in Pop you'll see Lemon by day and Midnight at night. Midnight is a dark ground with yellow shadows. The Glass switch sets where the glass effect goes: Off, On the menu or On the cards too. Next to it are the Blur and Opacity sliders. Back to the default puts you back on Pop, automatic colours and Space Grotesk. The Motion row sets how much moves on screen: Calm: only what you start moves. Lively: new things and feedback move once. Nothing repeats. Playful: there's slow movement in the background too, like the band of yesterday's reviews on Today. You can pause it anytime. Automatic: Playful, unless your device asks for less motion. Playful is only in the Pop style. Glass and Classic go up to Lively. If your device asks for less motion, nothing moves on its own, whatever you choose. At the Playful level, Pause motion stops all automatic movement at once. On a computer, click your name at the foot of the left-hand rail to find it; on a phone, it's at the bottom of More. The band of yesterday's reviews has its own Pause button too. Sounds is Off by default. Set it to On and you'll hear a short sound when you approve, skip, undo or switch something. It won't play on its own, and it won't tell you anything the screen doesn't. Under Keyboard shortcuts, the Single-key shortcuts (Replies, Reviews, jumps with g) switch controls single-letter commands on Válaszok (replies) and Értékelések (reviews), as well as go-to shortcuts starting with g. This switch applies only to the device where you change it. Ctrl + K, or Cmd + K on a Mac, opens search even when the switch is off. You'll find the keys in the article about search. You set the language of the pages with the Language menu, to Magyar or English. It sits next to Pause motion: click your name at the foot of the left-hand rail, or open More on a phone and scroll to the bottom. That's your own setting too. The daily report's language is separate. It comes from the Language field on the Account and team page of Settings, and it applies to everyone in the account.

s: Insiders see every feature, can write to Zsomb directly, and get a few tools for tracking down problems.
h: What you get Your notes The tools What doesn't change
b: The insiders' circle is for the people who try the app with us: the testers and the team. You become an insider by joining with an insider invite link. Only the team's own accounts can give one, as Inviting colleagues explains. Every feature. If something is switched on only in the team's own accounts, you see it as an insider in every account you're on. Nothing is gated like that yet, and the page says so. A direct line. On the More tab, the Insiders row opens a page. Under What should we improve? you can write what got in your way or what's missing, and add your name if you like. The note goes to Zsomb straight away, with the app's version attached. Tools for tracking down problems, under Tools. After Send, the page says “Got it. Zsomb will see it, and you can follow its status here.” Your notes are listed under Your notes, each with its status: Received, Seen or Done. Zsomb sets the status. You don't see other people's notes, and they don't see yours. You can send 30 notes an hour. During the test we also see which screens you open, and how often. Not what's on them. The app's version, the build and the name of the loaded bundle. If you're reporting a problem, these help a lot. Clear the cache and reload: clears the app's local store and its background worker, then reloads. It doesn't touch your account's data. Test push to this device: works when notifications are on for this device. If they aren't, the page tells you where to turn them on. Test Telegram message to yourself: goes to your own linked Telegram chat. Download my data: the same file you can download on the My login page. Download my Napló lines: your own Activity lines in this account, as a file. You can run 10 tests an hour. None of the tools writes a review, a reply, a report or an account setting. Nothing you do as an insider changes what customers see.

s: The Subscription page shows 3 packages. What goes in each, and what they'll cost, isn't final yet.
h: The three packages The band Add-ons Asking for a quote Billing details and invoices Usage
b: The packages are on the Subscription page, in the Account group of the left-hand rail, or under More on a phone. You can also get there from the Plan card, on the Subscription and data page of Settings. Only the account owner can choose a package. The Starter, Analyst and Full cards show what's in each one. Monitoring, the daily report and the written replies come with all three. What goes in each package, and the price, aren't final yet. That's why every package says “Price soon”. During the trial, everything works whichever package you're on. The page also shows how many active venues the account has, and which band that puts it in (1 venue, 2 to 9, or 10 or more). How the band affects the price isn't final yet. You can add Auto-answer to any package. Listing care and Competitor benchmark don't have a price yet, so they say “Coming soon”. Pick the package with the Choose this button, and tick the add-ons. Press the Request a quote button. We'll note what you picked. You won't pay anything here for now. If it's urgent, write to us with the Feedback button. On the Billing details card you tell us who to invoice: the company name, tax number, address, and the email address for invoices. The Invoices list is at the bottom of the page. We don't invoice during the trial. On the Subscription and data page of Settings, the Usage card shows how many reviews we fetched, and how many count checks, analysis runs and sent messages there were this month, last month and over the last 6 months. It shows counts only, with no price or cost.

s: Use a new account free for 14 days, with no bank card, on your own venues' real reviews.
h: What you get Where you see how far you are After the trial
b: The 14 days start from when you create the account. You don't need a bank card, and there's no minimum term. You get the full base package, working on your own venues' real reviews. We gather the reviews, write the replies, and prepare a daily report every day. We don't invoice you during the trial. You can add up to 5 venues during the trial, counting any you've switched off. If you hit the limit, the page tells you. If you need more, ask for a demo on the website, or write to us with the Feedback button. On a computer, click your name at the foot of the left-hand rail; on a phone, it's at the bottom of More. The Plan card, on the Subscription and data page of Settings, shows your plan and how many days you have left. It shows when the trial ends in your own time zone. In the last few days, a marker also shows up, in the left-hand rail on a computer or at the bottom of More on a phone. It takes you to the same page. Right now nothing stops when the trial ends. The daily report and everything else keep running. We haven't decided yet what the rule will be later. When we do, you'll read it here. For the packages, see Packages and billing.
